title: Add namespace fencing and restore idempotency helpers
author: Asha Mehta
description:
Motivation: Restores in private deployments occasionally collide with tenant activities (cron jobs, operator reconciliation) which can corrupt state if multiple restore attempts overlap. We need a low-friction guard that: (1) prevents concurrent restores inside the same tenant namespace, (2) makes restore operators idempotent so retries are safe, and (3) exposes short-lived fencing state for operator visibility and automation.

Summary: This PR introduces a namespace-level fencing CR annotation + a small lock controller used by the installer/restore controller. It also adds idempotency helpers for the restore flow (idempotency key generation, checkpoint markers, and safe-apply helpers). Helm chart changes wire the controller as a sidecar for the restore job; Terraform outputs include a new IAM role grant used for optional external locker backends.

What changed (high level):
- installer/restore/idempotency.go: helper functions to create idempotency keys, write idempotency checkpoints to S3-compatible object store, and verify replayability.
- controllers/namespace-fence/fence-controller.go: small controller that sets/clears the annotation and exposes fence status via a status subresource.
- helm/private/templates/restore-job.yaml: add fence sidecar container and env flags to enable idempotency checkpoints.
- docs/private/restore-runbook.md: updated runbook with new operator signals and step-by-step recovery flow.
- terraform/modules/installer/outputs.tf: export optional role/account for external lock plugins.
- e2e/tests/restore_fence_test.go: new tests that validate single-namespace fences and concurrent restore retry semantics.

Backwards compatibility: The fence is opt-in by default (installer flag enableNamespaceFence=false). When enabled the restore controller will acquire a fence annotation and fail fast if the namespace is already fenced. Operators upgrading from earlier releases without the flag will not change behavior.

Testing performed: unit tests for idempotency helpers (local mock S3), controller unit tests (fake client), and e2e that runs two parallel restores and verifies the second waits and then picks up the idempotency checkpoint rather than reapplying partial state. CI: all checks passed, including helm lint, go vet, unit tests and e2e smoke (see CI summary below).

Upgrade & rollback notes: Administrators can enable the fence feature via installer flag or Helm value. During rollback to older installer, fence annotations are tolerated (controller will be missing) — the runbook documents safe removal: clear fence annotations and delete any in-flight checkpoint objects. If a restore fails mid-flight, operator can re-run with the same idempotency key (exposed in restore controller logs) to resume.

Operational considerations: we added a short TTL (default 30m) for fences so a stuck controller won't lock namespaces indefinitely; long-running restores should extend the fence. The PR includes Prometheus metrics for fence_acquire_total and fence_held_seconds for alerting.

Related: ENG-9142 for orchestration cadence, SUP-7782 for incident notes where overlap caused data churn.

Checklist:
- [x] unit tests added
- [x] e2e test for concurrent restores
- [x] helm chart entries and linting
- [x] docs updated (runbook)
- [x] release notes entry

release_notes: Add optional namespace fencing for private restores to prevent concurrent restores from colliding.
Introduce idempotency helpers to allow safe restore retries and resume semantics.
Expose fence metrics for alerting and a short default TTL to avoid stuck locks.
